cards.front: Recall a key point about Purpose of Business and Enterprise
cards.back: Businesses provide goods (tangible products) and services (intangible products) to meet needs (essential) and wants (desirable but not essential).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Purpose of Business and Enterprise
cards.back: Factors of production: land (natural resources), labour (human effort), capital (man-made resources), enterprise (risk-taking and organisation).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Purpose of Business and Enterprise
cards.back: Opportunity cost: the benefit of the next best alternative foregone when making a decision - e.g. spending on new equipment means less available for marketing.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Purpose of Business and Enterprise
cards.back: Three sectors: primary (extraction), secondary (manufacturing), tertiary (services). The UK economy is now largely tertiary (approx 80%).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Purpose of Business and Enterprise
cards.back: Entrepreneur characteristics: risk-taker, creative, resilient, self-motivated, good communicator, decisive. Entrepreneurs spot gaps in the market and take calculated risks.

cards.front: What should you know about business exam tips?
cards.back: When discussing business purpose, use the SEE framework: Social benefits (jobs, community), Economic benefits (wealth, tax revenue), Enterprise benefits (innovation, choice). Always link back to the specific business context given in the question.

Students often make mistakes here. Wrong: All entrepreneurs are wealthy people who start businesses because they want to be rich. Correct: Entrepreneurs start businesses for many reasons beyond money: independence, passion for a product/service, desire to make a difference, flexibility, dissatisfaction with current employment.
